units.translation: I pray, pour out prayers, make vows

(with imperfect ηὐχόμην [I was praying] and aorist ηὐξάμην [I prayed], which in the manuscripts are mostly written without augment εὐχόμην εὐξάμην [I was praying, I prayed], like all other verbs of this kind, about which I have spoken in the Lexicon Sophocleum p. 199 and 202). It is said mostly of prayers made to the gods.
where I restored ηὔχετο [he was praying] from the copies.
thus I wrote for εὐξάμην [I prayed]
on which usage see Thes. vol. 3 p. 2523.

where Hermann restored εὐθυδίκαιοι [just in their dealings], Donaldson εὐχόμεθ᾽ [we pray]. In M is εὐθυδίκαι θ ' διδ'όιμεθ᾽ [just in their dealings ... we ...] (apostrophe after da added by a second hand in the margin ZT, i.e. ζήτει [look it up]).
pray that the tower ward off the enemy spear
pray for the better, that the gods be allies
and whoever before thought the gods nowhere then prayed with supplications
first I wish to pray to the gods
and I pray that from my hope it may fall
pray that the rest turn out well
the fated end remains long, but to those who pray it may come
I pray to this land and my father's tomb that this dream be fulfilled for me
and we always pray that other tributes of the land be born
it is necessary to pray to the Argives
and in the boundless ambush pray
you prayed to the gods, fearing to do these things thus
and I would have prayed for the trampling of many garments
and Hellas around the broad strait praying
who of mortals would ever pray to be born with an unharmed fortune
we pray that our race is from this land, inhabitants
who then is the heifer of Zeus that boasts it is gone from the cow
whence indeed our race, from the touch and inspiration of Zeus of the gadfly-driven cow, boasting, has been fulfilled
and we pray to be just in our dealings
rushing into battle with spirited boldness
the sweet-smelling fruit of the pale olive
lulling to sleep the sweet-smelling flame that consumes the offerings
Thus Scaliger from the scholia for συνωνύμων [of the same name].
and those who are by nature on the right and on the left
1η Μ ἐξωριάζειν [to banish], which was corrected from Hesychius and Photius, who explain εὐωριάζειν [to care little for] by ὀλιγωρεῖν [to care little for] and ἀφροντιστεῖν [to be unconcerned].
for it is grievous to care little for a father's words
and let no strife lay hold of the pledges
and Zeus, the toucher, with his hand begets offspring
become the much-remembering toucher of Io
one who sits by, reserve, third competitor
one who sits by, reserve, third competitor
Properly it is said of an athlete who sits by the contest, about to compete with the victor.
